title: Yachid, Echad, Kadmon: how the simple Essence holds every detail, like a nice guy's kindness
overview:
From chapter 10 to the end, the Mitteler Rebbe lays out the whole *hishtalshelus* in order, so that a person can trace anything in the world up to G-d and back down. But first one must contemplate its source, the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, and in detail. That sets up the chapter's paradox: *Yachid* means alone, with no parts, and yet the sources speak of ten *sefiros* there, even of a *Keser* and a *Malchus*. How can diversity come from simplicity?

The answer is the *hiyuli*. A nice guy's kindness is not a set of desires for coats and for shoes. It is one essence that includes every kindness he will ever be asked for, with its intellect, emotions, thought, speech and action, and none of them is there as a separate thing. So too a cat's power of movement, the soul's consciousness, and the light in the sun. From the *yechida* come three levels: the essence itself (*Yachid*), the power ready for a particular thing (*Echad*), and the deed fully estimated (*Kadmon*). Rabbi Walters calls chapters 10 to 13 the key to the whole book.

sections.title: From here to the end of the book: the four worlds in detail, and the Keser that unites each
sections.summary: The first nine chapters taught the method: trace a thing up the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent) to G-d and back down. Since not everyone knows the chain well enough, from chapter 10 the Mitteler Rebbe lays it out in order, down to the smallest subdivision, with the rule that the *Malchus* (kingship) of each level becomes the *Keser* (crown) of the next.

phrases.en: And now

phrases.he: הנה יש להבין דרך פרט בכל ד' עולמות דאבי''ע,
phrases.en: we have to understand the details of all of the four worlds of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*.

phrases.he: דהיינו בכל פרטי ענין עשר ספירות דאבי''ע
phrases.en: That means that we have to understand all the details of the ten *sefiros* of the worlds *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*:
their lights and their vessels,
how the lights go into the vessels, how the lights are enclothed in the vessels.

blocks.text: **And now**: chapters one through nine taught *hisbonenus* (contemplation) on the details of the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent): take a thing in the world and trace it up, stage by stage, to G-d Himself, then back down, until you recognize it again in the physical world and all the stages in between become transparent: "you realize that you're looking at G-d."

But as he said at the start of chapter 5, not everybody knows the *hishtalshelus* well enough for this, and scattered discourses do not give a working picture because they do not take it in order. So the Mitteler Rebbe wrote a book that does: this book, from chapter 10 to the end.

So, at least for those who do not know it yet, **we have to understand the details of all of the four worlds** of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* (Emanation, Creation, Formation and Action): the ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes) of each, **their lights and their vessels**, the difference between them and **how the lights are enclothed in the vessels.**

phrases.en: with all of their details:

phrases.he: גם בכל ספירה שמתחלקת לפרטי פרטיות
phrases.en: even how each *sefira* divides, subdivides into minute details, details after details, subdivision after subdivision.
Even, for example,

phrases.he: בבחינת חסד דמלכות שבחכמה שבמלכות דחסד
phrases.en: *chesed* of *Malchus* of *chachma* of *Malchus* of *chesed*,
and the like.

blocks.text:
**With all of their details**: how each *sefira* subdivides, to the fifth degree and beyond. Told that we are discussing **chesed of Malchus of chachma of Malchus of chesed**, you should be able to explain it, not just find it on the map.

At the first degree a person knows *chesed* means kindness. At the second, *chesed* of *gevura* (restraint) against *gevura* of *chesed*, most people are already lost. All this will be explained later. **And the like.**

phrases.he: וענין יחודם והתכללותם בבחינת הכתר שבכל עולם,
phrases.en: We also need to understand how the ten *sefiros* of each world are united and included in the *Keser* of each world,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת הממוצע בין עולם העליון לתחתון הימנו
phrases.en: The *Keser* of each world is the intermediary between an upper and a lower world.

blocks.text: **We also need to understand how the ten sefiros of each world are united and included in the Keser** (crown) **of each world**: their *yichud* and *hiskalelus* (unity and inclusion). The *Keser* of *Atzilus* is greater than its ten *sefiros* and includes them: have the *Keser* and you have everything. So too in *Beriya*. The *sefiros* of a world are nothing new to its *Keser*; they are its details, the *Keser* coming out in vessels.

blocks.title: Ten garments, ten pools of water
blocks.text: Chapters 23 and 24 will explain this: like one thing with ten garments, or ten pools of water, where you pour into the first and it spills over into the next.

And the *Keser* of each world is **the intermediary between an upper and a lower world**: the *Keser* of *Beriya* between *Atzilus* and *Beriya*, the *Keser* of *Atzilus* between *Atzilus* and the *ma'atzil* (the one who emanates).

phrases.en: as is known, the general rule, the general principle, which in short summarizes the way that the *hishtalshelus* goes:

phrases.he: שמבחינת מלכות שבעליון נעשה כתר לתחתון,
phrases.en: that from *Malchus* of a higher level is made the *Keser* of a lower level,
and that is true all the way up to the highest levels.

blocks.text: **As is known, the general rule**, which sums up the *hishtalshelus* in short: **from Malchus of a higher level is made the Keser of a lower level**, **all the way up to the highest levels**. That is why it is called a chain.

blocks.title: The links of a chain
blocks.text: *Hishtalshelus* means a chain: the lowest part of the upper link goes under the highest part of the lower one. So the *Malchus* of a higher level reaches a little below the *Keser* of the lower world, all the way up and down.

sections.title: The question: details, levels and sefiros in the simple Essence
sections.summary: Before the details of the chain, one must contemplate its source, the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* (the Essence of the infinite light) before the *tzimtzum* (contraction), and "even there" in detail: it has three levels, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon* (single, one and original), each with ten *sefiros*. But *Yachid* means alone, with no parts, so how can there be *sefiros* there, and how can diversity come from simplicity?

phrases.en: But first,

phrases.he: יש לכל מתבונן להתבונן במקור הראשון
phrases.en: it is first necessary for every person that's going to contemplate on G-dliness to contemplate on the first source where all of these things came from,
which is called the source of everything.

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: that is the essence of the infinite light
the way it is before the *tzimtzum* which is called the *makom panui*.

blocks.text: That first section introduced everything from here to the end of the book. Now the Mitteler Rebbe introduces this chapter itself, which explains the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* (the essence of the infinite light) before the first *tzimtzum* (contraction).

**But first**, before the details of how the worlds come out of G-d's light, **every person that's going to contemplate on G-dliness** has **to contemplate on the first source**, the *Mekora d'Kula*, **the source of everything.** We do not learn the *hishtalshelus* to know a Kabbalistic machine, but to see that it is really not there: it is G-d revealing Himself, and only looks like a chain because He made *tzimtzumim* and hid Himself, "like He's pulling a trick on us." The aim is to connect everything back to the first source.

That source **is the essence of the infinite light the way it is before the tzimtzum which is called the makom panui** (the empty place). The name belongs to the *tzimtzum*, not the light, and he says "the one called" because it is not really the first: there were *tzimtzumim* before it.

phrases.en: And even there, the essence of the infinite light before the *tzimtzum*, that also has to be understood in detail.
This is what is called elongating the *Echad*, dwelling on the *Echad*:
that you're supposed to dwell at length on G-d's simple unity.

blocks.text: **And even there, the essence of the infinite light before the tzimtzum, that also has to be understood in detail.** That already is a question: "Alarm should be going off in your head." How can there be details in what is simple? And this is no Chassidic trick: it is something you are supposed to do *al pi nigleh* (by the revealed law).

It is called *ma'arich b'echad*, **dwelling on the Echad**. Halacha requires lengthening *Echad* in *Shema*, but as we rule, the main thing is not saying it long: stretch the *ches* too much and it is like adding an *alef*, and that is not the word. So you say *Echad*, stress the *dalet*, then pause and contemplate: G-d is one, the *alef*, over the seven heavens and the earth, the *ches*, eight, and the four corners of the world. *Ma'arich b'echad* is thinking about that at length, in all its details.

**That you're supposed to dwell at length on G-d's simple unity** seems a contradiction: how can you think in detail about a plain fact with no details?

But *ma'arich* means to make it long, to explain it *b'arichus*, with many explanations. As chapter 1 says, the belief every Jew has in G-d's unity you should explain to yourself with many explanations and *meshalim* (analogies) until it is simple. How, when it is a simple thing? This is still the introduction, setting up a paradox we will live with for a while.

phrases.en: The simple unity is divided in general into three levels,
and each one of these three levels has ten *sefiros*.
These three levels are called *Yachid*, which means single, *Echad*, which means one, and *Kadmon*, which means original;

phrases.he: והכל בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and all of these three levels are all in the essence of the infinite light that precedes the first *tzimtzum* that we mentioned before.

blocks.text: So the *Atzmus Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, **the simple unity, is divided in general into three levels.** Divided into three? How does that make sense? We'll see. **And each one of these three levels has ten sefiros**: now we have thirty levels.

**These three levels are called Yachid, which means single, Echad, which means one, and Kadmon, which means original**: the origin everything after it needs. All three are in the *Atzmus Ein Sof* before the first *tzimtzum*, mentioned in chapter 9 and explained in 12 and 13. First he describes them, then gives *meshalim*.

phrases.en: *Yachid*, single, implies that it's alone.

phrases.he: והוא למעלה מהתאחדות נפרדים שנקרא אחד
phrases.en: So this is higher than the unity of parts, which is called *Echad*,
as is known.

blocks.text: **Yachid, single, implies that it's alone.** A *ben yachid* is an only son; a *ben echad* is just one son, implying there are others.

**So this is higher than the unity of parts, which is called Echad**, from *achdus*, different things united. *Echad* is a one with a two after it, or a one made of parts, like a thousand. *Yachid* is the only one, with no two and no parts, **as is known.**

blocks.title: One car
blocks.text: One car is a single unit made of many parts: wheels, chassis, body, doors, engine, carburetor, radiator. Missing a part, it is a car missing something, not really a car. That it can be divided shows it is not a real entity: "The car is just what you get when you put together a bunch of other things."

blocks.title: The computer
blocks.text: A computer is the same. Screens, typewriters, calculators and recording devices existed before it; its whole *chiddush* (novelty) is putting them together, not a new thing.

blocks.title: Pure olive oil
blocks.text: *Yachid* means a pure, elemental thing, not made of something else, like the bottle labeled "100% pure olive oil." Really anything physical divides into parts: oil into molecules, molecules into atoms. Physically nothing is totally *yachid*, and spiritually too only G-d is *Yachid*; everything else is made of parts, **as is known** from *Chovos HaLevavos* and other places.

phrases.en: So based on this,

phrases.he: בבחינת העצמות ממש לא יתכן לומר עדיין ענין עשר ספירות כלל
phrases.en: we cannot say that there's an idea of ten *sefiros* at all in G-d's essence, in the *Atzmus*.
like to say *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*;

phrases.he: שממילא מובן שקדם לזה בחינת כתר וחכמה כו'

blocks.text: **So based on this**, since G-d is *Yachid*, just Him, a higher unity than an *Echad* of parts, **we cannot say that there's an idea of ten sefiros at all in G-d's essence, in the Atzmus.**

It would be **like to say Malchus of the Ein Sof**, which implies a *Keser* and *chachma* before it. The *mashal* for *Malchus* is speech, and speech implies all the *sefiros*: a *ratzon* (will) to talk, a *sechel* (intellect) of what to say, and *middos* (emotions), since a happy person feels like talking and a sad one does not.

Yet G-d is totally singular, with nothing besides Him, so how can we speak of His *Malchus*, *Keser* and *chachma*? That is the basic question: sometimes we seem to put *sefiros* even in the *Atzmus*, and elsewhere we say, as makes sense, that there are none at all.

phrases.en: And the truth is,

phrases.he: גם בבחינת העצמות דאור אין סוף שנקרא לבדו
phrases.en: that even in the essence of the infinite light, which is called alone, the level of *Yachid*,
even there you can say that there are ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: אך שנקרא חכים לא בחכמה ידיעא
phrases.en: Only that we say that they are wise, and not with a knowable wisdom,
as is known,

phrases.he: עד ולאו מכל אלין מדות כלל.
phrases.en: really it has nothing to do with any of these *middos*.

blocks.text: **And the truth is that even in the essence of the infinite light, which is called alone, the level of Yachid**, with no parts, **even there you can say that there are ten sefiros.** How?

**Only that we say that they are wise, and not with a knowable wisdom, as is known**: there is *chachma* there, but not like your *chachma* or *bina* (understanding); **really it has nothing to do with any of these middos.** G-d is beyond all of them.

But that does not yet answer the question: if they are there, they are still divisions.

Why we are getting into this: to explain how the *hishtalshelus* and the ten *sefiros* come from the simple *Atzmus Ein Sof*. How can diversity come from simplicity? *Chassidus*, and really the Torah, says there is nothing but G-d revealing Himself in different ways. Then if G-d is simple, why do I see all these different things, a world that seems the opposite of revealing Him? This chapter shows how they come from Him.

sections.title: The answer in short: the light is as simple as the Essence, and the sefiros are there only as He estimated what would be
sections.summary: The light before the *tzimtzum* reveals the Essence exactly as it is, so it is as simple as the Essence: the *tehiru ila'a*, *Yachid*, one and not by the count of ten. We speak of *sefiros* there, a *Keser* and a *Malchus* even, only because of what He estimated in Himself would come about after the *tzimtzum*; the Essence is higher than them and yet includes them, like oil that floats above everything and permeates everything.

phrases.en: So what's the *inyan*?

phrases.he: דבאמת כמו שעצמות האין סוף הוא אור פשוט בתכלית הפשיטות,
phrases.en: that just like the essence of the *Ein Sof* is completely simple light,

phrases.he: כך ממש בחינת אורו וזיוו הנקרא אור אין סוף
phrases.en: so too, the light of the *Ein Sof* is also completely simple:

phrases.he: דהיינו הוא ושמו בלבד כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and this is what we said, that it's just G-d and His name alone.

blocks.text: **So what's the inyan?** **Just like the essence of the Ein Sof is completely simple light, so too, the light of the Ein Sof is also completely simple**, because light shows what it reveals the way it is, and it reveals the *Ein Sof* exactly as He is. **It's just G-d and His name alone**: Him, and His revelation of Himself to Himself, both totally simple.

phrases.en: And this is what is called the upper purity,

phrases.he: שזהו ענין ובחינת התגלות אור עצמותו כמו שהוא דוקא
phrases.en: that is the revelation of G-d's essence exactly the way He is.

blocks.text: **And this is what is called the upper purity**, *tehiru ila'a*: the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*. Pure, as with the olive oil, means nothing else in it: G-d and His name alone. The lower purity, after the *tzimtzum*, sees the world as revealing Him, but already as something separate, only connected with Him. The upper purity **is the revelation of G-d's essence exactly the way He is.**

phrases.en: And this is what's called *Yachid*, that it's alone,

phrases.he: שאין עוד מלבדו לומר בו לשון התאחדות
phrases.en: that there's nothing else, to say that there is an *achdus*, that there is a unification of parts,
*yichud* is like unite, that two things should unite.
This is what it says in *Pasach Eliyahu*, that You are one,
but not with a *cheshbon*, not with a calculation, not with a number.

blocks.text: **And this is what's called Yachid, that it's alone**: **there's nothing else, to say that there is an achdus, that there is a unification of parts.** *Achdus* is separate things working together, like Jews who keep their own ideas and sometimes disagree, but love each other. *Yichud* is two things becoming *mamash* (actually) one, like a father and mother who have a child, *basar echad* (one flesh). Neither fits here: there are no separate things to unite, "because it's just G-d."

**This is what it says in Pasach Eliyahu** (Elijah's opening prayer), **that You are one, but not with a cheshbon, not with a calculation, not with a number.** The Arizal explains which number: ten. G-d is not one made of ten *sefiros*; He is totally simple, because this is His revelation exactly as He is, the upper purity.

phrases.en: But this that we said,
that G-d is wise, but not with a knowable wisdom, etc.,

phrases.he: שיש על כל פנים חלוקי מדריגות,
phrases.en: that implies that there are divisions, that there are still different levels:
there's wise and understanding and kind and compassionate.
When we speak of these divisions, we don't mean that from the side of G-d's *etzem* there are these divisions;

phrases.he: רק מצד מה ששיער בעצמו בכח מה שעתיד להיות בפועל אחר הצמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: rather, when we speak of the ten *sefiros*, we mean that since G-d decided to make a world, and in the world He decided to make ten *sefiros* and to make a division between these things, so we say that they came from Him.

blocks.text: So how are ten *sefiros* there? **But this that we said, that G-d is wise, but not with a knowable wisdom**, **implies that there are divisions**: **there's wise and understanding and kind and compassionate.** If calling Him wise differs from calling Him understanding, there are divisions already. That His wisdom is not like mine does not help; "who cares if it's like my wisdom?" If this differs from that, it is a division, however far above my wisdom.

Not knowable means more than unlike our wisdom: as he says, nothing to do with these *middos* at all. You cannot even call it *chachma* or tell it from *bina*; it is just G-d. So why say they are there?
blocks.question: If the *sefiros* there are not a knowable wisdom, are wise and understanding, kind and compassionate not still divisions?

blocks.text: **When we speak of these divisions, we don't mean that from the side of G-d's etzem there are these divisions**, only from what He estimated in Himself would be after the first *tzimtzum*. Since He decided to make a world with ten distinct *sefiros*, **we say that they came from Him**; in their source they are not separate.

So when we say the *sefiros* are not in the *Atzmus*, we mean G-d is so far above them that you cannot say *chachma* or *bina* there. At the level of the *etzem* (essence), the essence of *chachma* is the essence of *bina*: just G-d. "The whole *hishtalshelus* is an artificial thing, and really our job is to see that it doesn't exist."

We want to see past the *hishtalshelus* to the *etzem*, that it is all G-d. But the way there goes through the details: see why and how they look different, realize they are not, and find the *etzem*.

blocks.title: Oil floats above and permeates
blocks.text: As *Kuntres Inyana shel Toras HaChassidus* ("On the Essence of Chassidus") and other places explain, the *etzem* is like oil, which floats above everything and also permeates everything: higher than the ten *sefiros*, yet in all of them.

blocks.title: An idea too deep to grab with your hand
blocks.text: Saying there are no ten *sefiros* there means G-d is higher than wisdom or anything. As *Tanya* says, calling G-d too great to understand is like calling an idea too deep to grab with your hand: it is like a joke.

On the other hand, we say the *sefiros* are there. Wisdom being absent does not mean, *chas v'shalom* (G-d forbid), that G-d is stupid; it is so far above wisdom that you cannot call it wisdom. And their being there means His existence, far above wisdom, includes it: "Because He's G-d, He automatically has wisdom." As the Rambam says, the first thing is to know there is a first Being, above everything, and everything comes out of His existence.

A *mashal* will show how this works. The basic idea: there is wisdom in the world, it came from somewhere, and only from G-d, so He must have wisdom. But in Him it is not wisdom as we know it, nor even to be called wisdom: a much higher thing where wisdom and understanding do not differ, which connects everything.

This chapter will explain it: a higher essence includes all the parts, and to it they are all the same, like oil that floats above everything and goes into everything. G-d's essence is above everything and so unknowable, yet found in everything, and a piece of the essence is the whole essence: His whole *etzem* is in *chachma*, in *bina*, and all the way down in a piece of cake or a tree.

In a way the whole rest of the book comes to explain this chapter, because it trains a two-step look at everything. First separate out the oil: G-d is higher than the thing, the thing is not G-d. Then reconnect: the real essence of the thing is G-d.

So with *chachma*: first, G-d is not wisdom and not love; He is higher. Then, wisdom really is a revelation of G-d, and you see everything that way. What this means will become clear as we do it through the book.

At the start of chapter 12 and the end of 13 he says this is the whole point of man and of this book: chapters 10 and 11, how the essence is above everything and everything reveals it; 12 and 13, how the *tzimtzum* makes things look separate from G-d while they are still Him. The rest is details: these four chapters are the key.

The basic point: G-d is above all these divisions, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, the ten *sefiros*, everything. Since after the *tzimtzum* He is revealed in levels, we say they came from before it, without defining levels there.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 10 opens by summing up lines 24-25, before it reads line 26.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקדש מלך בלשון האריז''ל עצמו ומבואר במקום אחר באריכות)

blocks.question: "Wait a minute, it says you're not allowed to talk about before the *tzimtzum*."
blocks.text: The text cites *Mikdash Melech*, in the Arizal's own words, to show this is nothing new. You will object that the Arizal's writings forbid speaking of before the *tzimtzum*: from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* and up, you cannot speak about it.

But the Arizal himself spoke about it. *Mikdash Melech* was written by a student of the Arizal ("Rabbi Yisrael Saruk, I think"), who made a *hanacha* (written record) of the Arizal's classes on before the *tzimtzum*, a subject Rabbi Chaim Vital's writings do not explain explicitly. So what we say about before the *tzimtzum* is usually quoted from *Mikdash Melech*.

And it explains it as we do now. You cannot speak of *mamash* (actual) levels there, a certain *chachma* or *bina*; but that it is higher than them and they came from there, you can. So this has a source in Kabbalah too.

phrases.he: וזהו ענין כללות המאמר הראשון בזוהר,
phrases.en: And this is also the intention of the very first sentence of the *Zohar*:

phrases.he: בריש הורמנא דמלכא גליף גליפו בטהירו עילאה
phrases.en: in the beginning of the sovereignty of the king, he engraved an engraving in the upper purity.

phrases.he: פירוש בעצמות גלוי אורו הפשוט הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: That in the essence of G-d's simple revelation of light that we mentioned before,
which is called the upper purity,
he engraved an engraving:
that's the idea of engraving letters.

blocks.text: **And this is also the intention of the very first sentence of the Zohar**, in some editions, which renders *Bereishis bara Elokim* ("In the beginning G-d created"): *B'reish hormanusa d'malka glif glifu b'tehiru ila'a*, **in the beginning of the sovereignty of the king, he engraved an engraving in the upper purity.** *Hormanusa* can also mean *ratzon* (desire), the beginning of the king's desire; keep both in mind, because he means both.

**That in the essence of G-d's simple revelation of light that we mentioned before**, **which is called the upper purity, he engraved an engraving**: **that's the idea of engraving letters.** *Glif*, like the English glyph in hieroglyphic, means letters.

phrases.en: And what does it mean, the beginning of the sovereignty, or the beginning of the *ratzon*, the beginning of his desire?
That means when it came up in his simple will to be king:
the beginning of the desire is the *Keser*, is the crown,

phrases.he: ובחינת האותיות שחקק הוא בחינת המלכות דאור אין סוף
phrases.en: and the letters that he engraved is the *Malchus* of the infinite light.

phrases.he: ואם כן יש ראש וסוף, כתר ומלכות,
phrases.en: That means that there's a beginning and an end, a *Keser* and a *Malchus*,

phrases.he: גם בבחינת עצמיות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: even in the essence of the infinite light.

blocks.text: **The beginning of the sovereignty, or the beginning of the ratzon**: **that means when it came up in his simple will to be king.** **The beginning of the desire is the Keser, is the crown, and the letters that he engraved is the Malchus of the infinite light.**

**That means that there's a beginning and an end, a Keser and a Malchus, even in the essence of the infinite light**, and in between *chachma* and *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura*. So the first *maamar* of the *Zohar* seems to put ten *sefiros* in the *Atzmus*. We already asked and answered this; he shows that the *Zohar*, like *Mikdash Melech*, is a source for the idea.

phrases.en: The explanation is
that it came up in G-d's simple thought and desire:
that I am going to be king,
but everything is still within Himself.

phrases.he: קודם ענין מה ששיער בעצמו בכח דוקא כל מה שיהיה לו רצון למלוכה בגלוי,
phrases.en: This is still before he had a *hashara* of how he's going to actually want to be king; in other words, how it's going to be revealed after the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: והוא אחר הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי כו'
phrases.en: The actual revelation of kingship is after the *tzimtzum* that's called the *makom panui*.

blocks.text: **The explanation is that it came up in G-d's simple thought and desire**, *Ana Emloch*, **that I am going to be king, but everything is still within Himself**, before any *hashara* (estimation) of how His kingship would be revealed: **the actual revelation of kingship is after the tzimtzum that's called the makom panui.**

So the *Zohar* says that in the *Atzmus*, the level of *Yachid*, there are a *Keser* and a *Malchus* even before He estimated what He would do after the *tzimtzum*. The levels are not actually there; but once He estimated the *hishtalshelus* with ten *sefiros*, we say He already had the *yecholes* (ability) for it before.

All this introduces what the chapter will explain: the *hiyuli* (raw potential), an essence higher than everything that includes everything. Kabbalah seems in some places to put ten *sefiros* there and in others to deny them. The answer: it is higher than them, but since they come out from it, it is not missing them; they are only not there the way they come out.

So far this is just a bunch of words that does not yet make much sense to us. So the Mitteler Rebbe gives *meshalim*, as he always does: first the idea in short with its Kabbalistic sources, then *meshalim* for it.

sections.title: The mashal: a nice guy's hiyuli desire for kindness
sections.summary: The powers of the soul, from will to action, are all hidden in the essence of the soul, the *yechida*. A kind person's *chafetz chesed* (desire for kindness) is a *hiyuli*, an essential power higher than any particular act, which includes every kindness he will ever be asked for, with all its intellect, emotions, thought, speech and action, totally united, until a situation draws one particular kindness out of it.

phrases.en: The likeness for this

phrases.he: ידוע מכחות הנפש בהתגלות מרצון עד המעשה
phrases.en: we can know from the powers of the soul, the way that they are revealed from the desire all the way until action:
that all of these soul powers, all of these different abilities and faculties and desires, all exist in detail, each one, every single one of them, not even one is missing,

phrases.he: בהעלם אור עצמות הנפש שנקרא בחינת יחידה
phrases.en: in the hidden light of the essence of the soul which is called *yechida*.

blocks.text: Now come analogies and examples. **The likeness for this**, *Yachid* above the ten *sefiros* yet holding them, **we can know from the powers of the soul, the way that they are revealed from the desire all the way until action.** Doing anything is a little *hishtalshelus*: you want it, think how, talk it over, do it, with emotions and intellect along the way. Ten powers.

**All of these soul powers** **all exist in detail, each one, every single one of them, not even one is missing,** **in the hidden light of the essence of the soul which is called *yechida*.** All these desires and abilities are already hidden in who you are.

phrases.en: Like for example,

phrases.he: כאשר האדם הוא חפץ חסד וטוב להטיב בדבר פרט,
phrases.en: if a person is a nice guy, and they want to do a nice thing, they have a desire to do a nice thing,

phrases.he: שזהו בא מצד שיש בו מדה זאת דחפץ חסד וטוב בבחינת עצמות נפשו, הנקרא יחידה
phrases.en: because he has this *midda*, this character trait of kindness, in the essence of his soul, which is called *yechida*.

phrases.he: על כן בא חפץ חסד זה בגלוי מן העלמו
phrases.en: And therefore, because he's a nice guy, this desire for kindness became revealed in this situation.

blocks.title: Hot cocoa, fuzzy slippers and a knock at the door
blocks.text: **Like for example, if a person is a nice guy.** A cold, snowy winter day; he sits with hot cocoa, a marshmallow in it, reading the paper. A knock. He gets up in his fuzzy slippers and opens the door on howling wind and a man shivering in tattered clothes. He brings him in, gives him cocoa and blankets by the fire, and asks what he needs. The man asks for a coat; he gives him a warm down coat and money for food and sends him off.

Why did he do it? Because he is a nice guy who likes to help people: **because he has this midda, this character trait of kindness, in the essence of his soul, which is called yechida**, the highest level of the soul.
**And therefore, because he's a nice guy, this desire for kindness became revealed in this situation.** A mean guy would have slammed the door, told him to get a job, or called security.

phrases.en: We must say,
with certainty,
that this desire for kindness, the way that it's included in the essence of his soul,
is in a way that is called a *hiyuli* power in his self,

phrases.he: לכלול כל מה שעתיד לחפוץ בחסד וטוב
phrases.en: and it includes everything that he is ever going to desire in goodness and kindness,

phrases.he: בכל פרטי פרטי הענינים שיבקשו ממנו
phrases.en: with all the little, little detail things that are going to be asked from him.

blocks.text: **We must say, with certainty, that this desire for kindness, the way that it's included in the essence of his soul, is in a way that is called a hiyuli power in his self.** *Hiyuli* means an essence, totally simple and above any particular form, and so able to come out in anything.

It is an essential power, **and it includes everything that he is ever going to desire in goodness and kindness, with all the little, little detail things that are going to be asked from him**, not a separate desire for each favor he will be asked.

blocks.title: The two beggars on the park bench
blocks.text: There is no desire for coats beside a desire for something else. Next day the man with the coat sits on a park bench beside a friend whose shoes are flapping, soles off, snow getting in, and sends him to the nice guy. The friend does not need a coat; he needs shoes. The kindness, he is told, was never a kindness for coats: "His kindness isn't for anything." Then, says the friend, he surely does not need him.

blocks.title: His kindness isn't for anything
blocks.text: Not for anything means higher than anything, a *hiyuli*: his kindness is for whatever will be kind. Shoe or coat, it is all the same; whatever is kind in the situation, it will come into, even things you would not think kind: if he is a surgeon, into cutting people up, "cuz sometimes that's kind." So it is an essence that includes every detail he will ever be asked for, though they are not *mamash* there.

phrases.en: If so,
we must say

phrases.he: שקודם שעלה ברצונו וחפצו זה שבגלוי, להטיב חסדו בדבר זה הפרטי,
phrases.en: that before he had a desire to help this person in this particular way, to give him a coat,

phrases.he: היה כלול בעצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי
phrases.en: this desire was already included in the essence of his *hiyuli* power of kindness, in his essential power of kindness within himself.
And then, when the situation arises that the person needs the coat, it goes out from the essence,
and now it becomes revealed in this situation by being kind in that way.

blocks.text: **If so, we must say that before he had a desire to help this person in this particular way, to give him a coat, this desire was already included in the essence of his hiyuli power of kindness.** That is what kindness is: a nice person in such a situation will do this.

**And then, when the situation arises that the person needs the coat, it goes out from the essence, and now it becomes revealed in this situation by being kind in that way.** Elsewhere a coat might be mean; here a kind person has to give it. So real kindness is an essence that includes everything: he will want to do any and every kind thing that comes up.

Missing even one *prat* (detail), it is not real kindness but an organization, a foundation: a system that gives out coats and tells someone who needs shoes, "Sorry, we don't give shoes." A worker may be nice and help him, and it may do good, but a person could die of starvation on the doorstep and the foundation cannot help him; that is not what it does. It is a machine, with no essence of kindness, because there is no person there with a desire to be kind. Real kindness comes out in whatever would be kind: if he needs food, you give him food too.

sensitivity.reason: A sharp generalisation about charitable foundations as machines that let a person starve on the doorstep.
sensitivity.publishable: Missing even one *prat* (detail), it is not real kindness but a system: a system that gives out coats and tells someone who needs shoes, "Sorry, we don't give shoes." A worker may be nice and help him, and it may do good, but it has no essence of kindness, because there is no person there with a desire to be kind. Real kindness comes out in whatever would be kind: if he needs food, you give him food too.

blocks.text: Someone who will do everything for you except give you shoes is not kind. If you really care, you want to do whatever the person needs. Maybe he has some thing about shoes; that is something else stopping him. As far as the kindness goes, he wants to do whatever the person needs.
So the kindness includes everything, and must include every detail or it is not kindness. Yet the details are not *mamash* there, no desire for a coat and another for shoes: it is just kindness.

phrases.en: And we see

phrases.he: שיש בחפץ חסד זה שכל וחכמה ומדות ומחשבה ודבור ומעשה
phrases.en: that when this desire for kindness is revealed, when he actually wants to do something nice, there's an intellect, and there's a wisdom, and there are emotions, and there's thought, speech, and action.

blocks.text: **And we see that when this desire for kindness is revealed**, **there's an intellect, and there's a wisdom, and there are emotions, and there's thought, speech, and action**: a whole process of sizing up the situation and figuring out what will be kind in it.

You need a *bissel sechel* (a little intellect). You can mean well, but a strong desire to be really kind develops some smarts, because otherwise your help does more harm than good. Part of wanting to be kind is wanting to be smart about it.

There is a kind way of understanding, which looks for the good, for merit and help for a person, where a mean person looks for fault and reasons to punish: a kind *sechel*, a worldview. And there is a wisdom, a creativity that finds solutions to people's problems: you need *chachma*.

Then the emotions. You feel for the person, and that includes fear and hate of whatever opposes the kindness: help the starving and you hate hunger and what causes it. You overcome obstacles, *netzach* (victory); you glorify kindness, like *tiferes* (beauty); you laud the people who do it, with prizes and honor, so others want to. A kind person relates to everything in the world in a certain way.

Your priorities determine your emotions, so being for kindness gives a certain set of them. Then thought, speech and action: think what to do, invite the poor man in, ask what size coat he wears. And the main thing is the *maaseh* (action): actually give him the coat.

phrases.en: If so,

phrases.he: ודאי במקור חפץ חסד זה בהעלמו, כשהיה כלול בעצמיות החפץ חסד ההיולי, גם כן מהתחלקות שכל ומדות ומחשבה דבור ומעשה שבו
phrases.en: so we must say that included in the identity of kindness, his essential kindness, is already: if you know what it means to be kind, you already know how to think kind, how to feel kind, how to speak kind, how to do kind; you know how to do everything.

phrases.he: אבל בבחינת עצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי, כמו שהוא קודם שבא עדיין בדבר פרטי,
phrases.en: nevertheless, the way that these things are in the self of the essential kindness, before it comes to a particular thing,

phrases.he: הגם שבודאי גם שם יש התחלקות שכל ומדות כו',
phrases.en: even though even at that stage we must say that it includes intellect and emotions,
nevertheless, all these details, even though we must say that they're there, they're totally unified and they're included.

blocks.text: **If so**, **we must say that included in the identity of kindness, his essential kindness, is already**: **if you know what it means to be kind, you already know how to think kind, how to feel kind, how to speak kind, how to do kind; you know how to do everything.** Being a nice person, he has the *sechel* and *middos* for it automatically.

**Nevertheless, the way that these things are in the self of the essential kindness, before it comes to a particular thing**, when you are just a kind person: **even at that stage we must say that it includes intellect and emotions**. Kindness that does not come into how he understands, feels, thinks, speaks and acts is not real kindness.

There is a *halacha*: giving a lot of *tzedaka* (charity) with a sour face, making the poor man feel like dirt, is much worse than giving a little with kind words. The main thing in kindness is not the donation but the attitude: you care about him and do not feel superior; if anything, he is doing you the favor.

That is why it is called *tzedaka*, righteousness: you are only doing what is right. Nobody deserves to go hungry, and if you have food for two, the economy gave you his share too. And from the Torah's point of view, G-d made some rich and some poor so you can do the *mitzva*: he suffers so you can do it, "so you really owe him big time." And the wheel of fortune turns; you could be in his shoes.

You cannot act or talk kindly without sincerely feeling it, and that comes only from this understanding of your relation to the person, your money, your success. Without it, helping feels like a bother, you resent giving, and it comes out badly. So being kind includes all these details; if it does not come out in all of them, it is not really kindness.

**Nevertheless, all these details, even though we must say that they're there, they're totally unified and they're included.** They have no existence of their own, not a set of separate things he must also have: "If you have kindness, you have everything."

sections.title: Every attribute is a hiyuli, and all ten are simply the self
sections.summary: Justice, beauty, victory and kingship are each a *hiyuli* like kindness, holding all their details united, as Napoleon's will to rule was in him as a baby. And the ten essential attributes themselves are not ten things united in the *yechida*: they are not separate from the essence at all. There is just you, the human essence, expressed in different arenas.

phrases.en: And the same way with a different character trait
within yourself,
like the attribute of *gevura*, which is, let's say, severity, or justice,
and the same thing with beauty, or showing off,
and the same thing with winning, with victory, competition,
and the like,
all the way down to the desire for kingship,
that's the attribute of upliftedness;
that surely the attribute of kingship, of leadership, includes all ten things:
there's desire, *chafetz*, which means like a craving, to be a king,

and there's a whole creative wisdom that you have to have of how you're going to make the laws and how you're going to run your country, and then there's the emotions, and there's thought, speech, and action.

blocks.text: **And the same way with a different character trait within yourself, like the attribute of gevura, which is, let's say, severity, or justice**: wanting everything fair. A sense of justice includes every detail: in every situation he will want the fair thing, things deserved and worked for. A whole worldview comes with it.

**And the same thing with beauty, or showing off**: a person with a sense of beauty knows how to make everything beautiful. **And the same thing with winning, with victory, competition**: a competitive person wants to win everything, without a separate desire for each game.
**And the like, all the way down to the desire for kingship, that's the attribute of upliftedness**, *hisnasus*: to be over people, in charge, praised by subordinates.

Surely **the attribute of kingship, of leadership, includes all ten things**: **there's desire, chafetz, which means like a craving, to be a king**, and **a whole creative wisdom** of how to make the laws and run the country, emotions, thought, speech and action. A lot goes into being a king.

phrases.he: אך קודם שבא לבחינת התגלות בדבר פרט,
phrases.en: But before the attribute of kingship is revealed in a particular thing,
like to be king of this country,

phrases.he: כלולים ומתאחדים בתכלית בבחינת מדת המלוכה ההיולית העצמית
phrases.en: all these details were included and united completely in the central attribute of kingship within himself,

phrases.he: כמו בעצמות חפץ חסד ההיולי הנ"ל
phrases.en: just like we spoke about the essential power of kindness in yourself.

blocks.title: Napoleon as a baby
blocks.text:
Take a great king and world dictator like Napoleon, who conquered Europe and started on Russia: a great desire to be king and a great intellect for it, his laws, a whole theory of how countries should run. All those details are only how it came out in practice, like a kind person's coat.

From birth he had the desire to be king, or he would not have wanted it later; but as a baby he had none of the details. "He didn't even know what country he was in."
blocks.outOfPlace: He gives the mashal just before he reads line 46, which it illustrates.

blocks.text: **But before the attribute of kingship is revealed in a particular thing, like to be king of this country**, France and then the world, **all these details were included and united completely in the central attribute of kingship within himself**: the part of him that is a leader.

Every person has it, some much more, and it can come out in running the eighth-grade yearbook or ruling France: being on top, with others recognizing your supremacy and listening to you. As the book says later, it shows even in a little kid who pushes a dog's head down and sits on it. But kingship is mainly over people who are otherwise your equals.
blocks.title: The yearbook and the dog

blocks.text: **Just like we spoke about the essential power of kindness in yourself**: as kindness includes all the shoes and coats, kingship includes all the countries. The details are not really there; it is a higher essence, and if you have it, they come out by themselves.

So what is each power of the soul? Kindness is not a set of details but one essence, that you are kind, part of who you are, and the details come out automatically. So with justice, beauty, victory and kingship. Every person has all ten and brings them out in his own ways, and that is his individual identity.

phrases.en: If so, it's understood automatically

phrases.he: שבחינת מדת העצמיות דכח''ב וחג''ת ונהי''ם ההיולים שבעצמיות הנפש,
phrases.en: that all ten of the essential powers, attributes of yourself: your desire and wisdom and understanding and kindness and severity and beauty and victory and glory and *yesod*, which is like the idea of your relationship, and your kingship, your leadership ability,

phrases.he: לא יתכן לומר גם לשון זה שמתאחדים וכלולים בעצמיות הנפש הנקרא יחידה
phrases.en: we can't even say that these are ten different attributes that have distinct identities and that they're just somehow united and included within the essence of your soul, which is called the *yechida*, within your inner self.

blocks.text: **If so, it's understood automatically that all ten of the essential powers, attributes of yourself** (desire, wisdom, understanding, kindness, severity, beauty, victory, glory, *yesod*, which is like your relationships, and kingship) are what you actually are as a human being, not just your self-image. **We can't even say that these are ten different attributes that have distinct identities and that they're just somehow united and included within the essence of your soul, which is called the yechida.** No kind part and wise part are put together to make you. "Really, there's just you."

So by just being yourself, as they always tell you, it all comes out. You need not impress anyone that you are kind or wise. As shoes and coats come out of kindness, wisdom and kindness come out of being yourself, because the essence of each attribute is just you.

Further, as there is an essence of kindness, there is an essence of what a person is. That human factor comes out in the intellect as wisdom and in the emotions as kindness and justice, because these are human attributes: "People are kind. Rocks aren't kind." So all the attributes are like shoes and coats: one human element in different arenas.

Each person also has his own twist on the human element, so if he is just himself he will know how to act in each situation. But at the core, by being a person he has all ten, not as separate things put together: there is something higher, that he is a person, and in the intellect it comes out as creativity and logic.

Like the sci-fi books and movies that try to build artificial intelligence, robots with every characteristic: some things a programmed thing cannot get without an essence, a soul, the human element. "You can't teach a computer humor." A computer computes, so it has intellect, but not human intellect. So all ten attributes are one essence, the human element, applied in different ways.

He is showing an essence, a *hiyuli*: a point higher than the details, which has all of them. He showed it with kindness, said the same of every attribute, then went higher: kindness is the essence of all kind deeds, justice of all just deeds, and the human essence unites all ten attributes.

blocks.text: Go further and you go higher. Behind the human element, the animal, the plant, the angels and everything is an essence: the G-dly essence. You can keep going higher even within G-dliness, to how it is revealed in the ten *sefiros*, but that is for the next chapter.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 14 opens by summing up class 13 (lines 46-48) and the kindness mashal before it, then reads line 49; placed under line 48, which it restates.

blocks.text: So: first an essence shown in a simple, concrete example, kindness and its shoes and coats; then how the essence of the soul relates to all ten attributes. The ten are really one, not separate things uniting in the *yechida*.
